exercises.name: Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell)

source_english.description: Hold a dumbbell and support, raise one heel from the step, lower it below the step, then change legs.
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step or platform with your heels hanging off and your toes on the step.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and place your other hand on a wall or railing for support.
Raise your heel as high as possible, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down below the step.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
form_cues: Keep the ankle over the second toe.
common_mistakes: Pushing off with the other leg.
source_english.safety_note: Use a handhold or machine support and keep the ankle moving vertically.

exercises.name: Sissy Squat (Weighted)

source_english.description: A weighted sissy squat keeps the torso leaning back as the knees travel forward and the heels stay lifted.
instructions: Hold one weight plate against the chest and stand with feet hip-width apart.
Rise onto the balls of the feet, brace the abdomen, and lean the torso back in a straight line.
Bend the knees forward and lower the body while keeping the hips extended and knees tracking the toes.
Drive through the balls of the feet to return upright without folding at the hips.
form_cues: Keep the torso and hips aligned.
Let the knees follow the toes.
Use a shallow depth if the heels or knees cannot stay controlled.
common_mistakes: Sitting the hips back like a regular squat.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light plate and a support nearby because the forward knee travel challenges balance.

exercises.name: Sit Up (Weighted)

source_english.description: A weighted sit-up adds a light plate held at the chest to the same controlled trunk-flexion path.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hold a plate against the chest.
Brace the abdominals and curl the torso toward the knees while keeping the plate close.
Continue until the trunk reaches a comfortable upright position without rounding the neck.
Lower the back slowly until the shoulders touch the floor.
form_cues: Keep the plate against the sternum.
Use the abdominals to initiate the curl.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a light plate that will not shift toward the face or abdomen.

exercises.name: Step Up

source_english.description: A step-up places one foot on a box or platform and drives the body upward through that leg.
instructions: Stand facing a stable box with feet hip-width apart.
Place the whole right foot on the box and lean slightly over that leg.
Drive through the right foot to stand on the box, then step down under control.
Repeat on the other leg, keeping the knee aligned with the toes.
form_cues: Use the whole foot on the box.
common_mistakes: Pushing off hard from the floor leg.
Using a box that is too high.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a box height that permits a stable step and keep the landing area clear.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat (Kettlebell)

source_english.description: Sumo Squat (Kettlebell) uses one kettlebell held at the chest while a wide, turned-out stance guides the hips down between the knees.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than shoulder width and toes turned slightly out.
Hold one kettlebell by the horns at the chest and brace the abdomen.
Bend the hips and knees, lowering the pelvis between the thighs while heels stay down.
Drive through both feet to stand tall and reset.
common_mistakes: Dropping the bell away from the chest.
source_english.safety_note: Use a kettlebell you can keep close while maintaining the wide stance.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge (Sandbag)

source_english.description: Walking Lunge (Sandbag) alternates forward steps while a sandbag stays secured against the torso.
instructions: Hold the sandbag against the chest with both arms and stand tall.
Step forward with the right foot and lower until both knees bend and the right heel stays down.
Drive through the right foot and bring the left foot forward.
Alternate legs while keeping the sandbag close.
source_english.safety_note: Use a sandbag that stays secure and a clear lane for the walking steps.

exercises.name: Wrist Roller

source_english.description: Wrist Roller winds a suspended weight up and down by alternating wrist flexion and extension.
instructions: Hold the wrist-roller bar with both hands at shoulder height and arms extended.
Roll the bar forward with alternating wrist turns until the weight reaches the hands.
Pause briefly at the top without shrugging.
Reverse the wrist direction to lower the weight slowly to the floor.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the hanging weight clear of feet and use a light load that can be reversed safely.
